c-sd-basic.label: Speed, distance and time: units first
c-sd-basic.summary: One formula and one habit: write minutes and hours in the same unit before dividing.

c-sd-relative.label: Relative speed: meeting and chasing
c-sd-relative.summary: Towards each other speeds add; in the same direction they subtract.

c-sd-circular.label: Overtaking on a track
c-sd-circular.summary: The faster one overtakes after closing the gap between them at the relative speed.

q-sd-convert.label: Same distance, different time or route
q-sd-convert.summary: Distance changes by a percentage, time is fixed, find the new speed.

q-sd-units.label: A rate in short time scaled to a long time
q-sd-units.summary: Distance in 1 minute; find the distance in hours.

q-sd-meet.label: Two bodies meet: opposite or same direction
q-sd-meet.summary: Two meeting times give two equations: sum and difference of speeds.

q-sd-overtake.label: First overtake on a circular track
q-sd-overtake.summary: Gap ÷ relative speed gives the time; times the faster speed gives the distance.

c-sd-train.label: Trains: crossing poles, platforms and each other
c-sd-train.summary: A train crossing something covers its own length plus that object's length at its speed; two trains use the relative speed.

c-sd-avg.label: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time
c-sd-avg.summary: Never average the speeds. Add the distances, add the times, divide.

c-sd-late.label: Changing the speed: arriving early or late
c-sd-late.summary: Speed and time are inverse; the gap between two journey times (early + late) fixes the distance.

c-sd-race.label: Races: beats by, starts and ratios of speeds
c-sd-race.summary: Convert 'beats by 100 m' into the ratio of distances run in the same time, then chain the ratios.

q-sd-basic.label: Distance, speed and time, with units and fractions
q-sd-basic.summary: One formula; turn minutes into hours, fractions of a journey into km, and keep clock times honest.

q-sd-ms.label: Converting km/h to m/s and back

q-sd-wheel.label: Wheel turns, circumference and speed
q-sd-wheel.summary: One turn covers the circumference π d; distance = turns × π d.

q-sd-ratio.label: Ratios of speeds, times and distances
q-sd-ratio.summary: Speed ∝ distance ÷ time: divide the distance ratio by the time ratio.

q-sd-angle.label: Two walkers at right angles
q-sd-angle.summary: Distances travelled are the two legs of a right triangle; use Pythagoras or the 3-4-5, 5-12-13 triples.

q-sd-chase.label: Policeman and thief, one overtakes the other
q-sd-chase.summary: Head start ÷ (faster − slower) is the time to catch up.

q-sd-relative.label: A train passing a man or vehicle that is moving
q-sd-relative.summary: Same direction: subtract the speeds; opposite: add. The train's length is covered at that speed.

q-sd-lap.label: Runners on a track meet again at the start
q-sd-lap.summary: They are together again at the start after the LCM of the lap times.

q-sd-pole.label: A train crossing a pole or a man standing
q-sd-pole.summary: Distance covered = the train's own length.

q-sd-platform.label: A train crossing a platform, bridge or standing train
q-sd-platform.summary: Distance = train + platform; the extra time over a pole crossing is the platform's time.

q-sd-trains.label: Two trains crossing each other
q-sd-trains.summary: Opposite: add the speeds; same direction: subtract; the distance is the sum of the lengths.

q-sd-average.label: Average speed over unequal stretches
q-sd-average.summary: Total distance ÷ total time; 2uv/(u + v) for equal distances.

q-sd-late.label: A change of speed makes him early or late
q-sd-late.summary: D/v1 − D/v2 = the total time gap (late + early). Test the options.

q-sd-race.label: A beats B by, start and finishing ratios
q-sd-race.summary: Distances run in the same time give the ratio of speeds; chain A : B and B : C.

formulas.note: Put minutes and hours in one unit first.

formulas.text: Same time: speed ∝ distance     Same distance: speed ∝ 1 ÷ time
formulas.note: 25% more distance in the same time needs 25% more speed.

formulas.text: Opposite: relative speed = u + v     Same direction: = u − v
First overtake: time = gap ÷ (u − v); distance by the faster = u × time
formulas.note: The track length matters only if the gap is more than one lap.

formulas.text: Train crossing: pole = own length; platform or another train = both lengths; at speed (own or relative)
formulas.note: Opposite: u + v. Same direction: u − v.

formulas.text: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time. Equal distances: 2uv ÷ (u + v)
formulas.note: 40 and 60 km/h over equal distances average 48, not 50.

formulas.text: D/v1 − D/v2 = time gap; D = (v1 v2 ÷ (v2 − v1)) × time gap
formulas.note: Late by 6 min then early by 6 min means a 12-minute gap.

formulas.text: 'A beats B by d in a race of L' means A : B = L : (L − d) as distances in the same time
formulas.note: Chain the ratios: A : C = (A : B) × (B : C).

formulas.text: After two bodies meet and reach each other's start in t1 and t2: speed ratio = √(t2 : t1)
formulas.note: Trains from A and B that reach B and A 4 h and 9 h after meeting: ratio √(9/4) = 3 : 2.

q-sd-convert.cue: 'Distance increases by 25%… must still arrive in the same time. New speed?'
q-sd-convert.standard: Same time, so speed grows with distance: 200 × 1.25 = 250 km/h.
q-sd-convert.fast: The 40 minutes cancels. Raise the speed by the same 25%: 200 + 50.
q-sd-convert.eliminate: More distance in the same time means a higher speed, so the answer is above 200, and 25% of 200 is exactly 50.
traps: Taking 25% of the time instead of the distance.
Working out time from the 40 minutes and not cancelling it.

q-sd-units.cue: 'A train covers 1.2 km in 1 minute. How far in 2 h 15 min?'
q-sd-units.eliminate: 1.2 km a minute is 72 km/h. In 2.25 hours that is between 72 × 2 = 144 and 72 × 2.5 = 180, and 72 × 2.25 is exactly 162.
traps: Reading 2 h 15 min as 2.15 hours.
Treating 1.2 km as 1.2 km/h without the minute.

q-sd-meet.cue: Two bodies start a fixed distance apart; one meeting time towards each other and another in the same direction.
q-sd-meet.standard: Towards: u + v = 480 ÷ 5 = 96. Same direction: u − v = 480 ÷ 15 = 32. So u = (96 + 32) ÷ 2 = 64.
q-sd-meet.fast: The faster speed is the average of the sum and the difference: (96 + 32)/2.
q-sd-meet.eliminate: The faster speed must exceed half the sum (48) and be less than the sum (96). Test each option: v = 96 − u must be below u and u − v must equal 32.
traps: Taking 96 as the faster speed.
Using 480 ÷ 15 as one of the speeds.
Choosing the slower speed, 32, as the answer.

q-sd-overtake.cue: A circular track, two starts with the second ahead by some distance, and 'when does he overtake for the first time'.
q-sd-overtake.standard: Relative speed 20 − 8 = 12 m/s. Gap 500 m, so time = 500 ÷ 12. Distance of the motorcycle = 20 × 500/12 = 833.33 m.
q-sd-overtake.eliminate: The motorcycle covers more than the 500 m gap (it must close it at 12 of its 20 m/s), so it travels about 500 × 20/12 ≈ 833 m. 800 m is too short and 1,800 m is far too long.
traps: Giving the truck's distance (333.33 m) rather than the motorcycle's.
Adding the speeds, as if they met head on.
Using the track length of 2.2 km, which is irrelevant here.

q-sd-basic.cue: 'He walks 5 km/h for 15 minutes; how far?' or 'a journey in several parts, find the missing speed'.
q-sd-basic.standard: Distance = speed × time with minutes turned into hours; for 'the rest of the journey' work out the part left and the time left.
q-sd-basic.fast: Use the unit that makes the numbers whole (m/s for seconds, km/h for hours).
q-sd-basic.eliminate: Check the answer's size: a man cannot walk more than about 6 km in an hour, and 5 km/h for 15 minutes is a little over 1 km.
traps: Mixing minutes with hours.
Using the whole journey instead of the part remaining.

q-sd-ms.cue: 'A car goes 10 m in a second. Its speed in km/h?'
q-sd-ms.fast: Multiply m/s by 3.6, or divide km/h by 3.6.
q-sd-ms.eliminate: km/h is always the larger number: if your answer is smaller than the m/s you started with, you converted the wrong way.
traps: Using 5/18 in the wrong direction.
Converting only part of the data.

q-sd-wheel.cue: 'A wheel of diameter 70 cm turns 400 times a minute. Speed of the car in km/h?'
q-sd-wheel.standard: Circumference = π d = 22/7 × 70 = 220 cm; distance per minute = 400 × 220 cm; convert to km an hour.
q-sd-wheel.fast: Pick the π value so that the diameter cancels (22/7 with a multiple of 7).
q-sd-wheel.eliminate: 52.8 km/h is the only reasonable speed for a car; 528 and 0.528 are off by powers of ten.
traps: Using the radius as the diameter.
Powers of ten when moving from cm to km.

q-sd-ratio.cue: 'A truck covers 550 m a minute, a bus 33 km in 45 minutes. Ratio of speeds?'
q-sd-ratio.standard: Put both in km/h (33 and 44), then reduce 33 : 44 = 3 : 4. For times: time ∝ length ÷ speed.
q-sd-ratio.fast: Speed ratio = distance ratio ÷ time ratio, term by term.
q-sd-ratio.eliminate: The ratio must come out in the order asked (first to second): an inverted ratio is the usual wrong option.
traps: Giving the time ratio when the speed ratio is asked.
Comparing speeds in different units.

q-sd-angle.cue: 'Two cars leave a point at right angles at 36 and 48 km/h. Distance after 15 seconds?'
q-sd-angle.standard: Legs 150 m and 200 m; distance = √(150² + 200²) = 250 m.
q-sd-angle.eliminate: The hypotenuse is longer than either leg and shorter than their sum (350): strike 400 and 150.
traps: Adding the legs (350).
Forgetting to convert km/h to m/s.

q-sd-chase.cue: 'A policeman is 200 m behind a thief; he runs 11 km/h, the thief 10 km/h.'
q-sd-chase.standard: Gain per hour = 11 − 10 = 1 km; in 6 minutes he gains 100 m; 100 m remain.
q-sd-chase.fast: Time to catch = head start ÷ (faster − slower); distance run = time × speed.
q-sd-chase.eliminate: The gap shrinks but does not vanish unless the time is long enough: compare the time with head start ÷ speed difference.
traps: Adding the speeds.
Answering the time when the distance covered is asked (or the reverse).

q-sd-relative.cue: 'A 500 m train at 63 km/h passes a man walking at 3 km/h in the same direction.'
q-sd-relative.standard: Relative speed = 63 − 3 = 60 km/h = 50/3 m/s; time = 500 ÷ 50/3 = 30 s.
q-sd-relative.fast: Subtract for the same direction, add for the opposite direction; length ÷ relative speed.
q-sd-relative.eliminate: Passing a man moving the same way takes longer than passing a standing man: the time must exceed length ÷ train speed.
traps: Adding when the directions are the same.
Forgetting to convert km/h to m/s before dividing metres.

q-sd-lap.cue: 'Four runners take 40, 50, 60 and 30 minutes a round. When do they meet again at the start?'
q-sd-lap.standard: LCM of the lap times = 600 minutes = 10 hours; add to the start time.
q-sd-lap.fast: LCM first, then convert to clock time.
q-sd-lap.eliminate: The answer is a multiple of every lap time: strike any time that is not.
traps: Taking the HCF.
Adding the start time in the wrong unit.

q-sd-pole.cue: 'A 100 m train at 30 km/h passes a man standing near the line. Time?'
q-sd-pole.fast: Length ÷ speed in m/s; or speed 12 m/s = 120 ÷ 10 when seconds are given.
q-sd-pole.eliminate: 30 km/h is about 8 m/s, so 100 m takes about 12 s: strike 10 and 15 on a quick estimate.
traps: Leaving the speed in km/h.
Adding a platform length that is not there.

q-sd-platform.cue: 'A train passes a 50 m platform in 14 s and a man standing on it in 10 s. Its speed?'
q-sd-platform.standard: The extra 4 s cover the platform's 50 m: speed = 12.5 m/s = 45 km/h.
q-sd-platform.fast: Platform length ÷ difference of the two times is the speed; speed × time for a pole is the train's length.
q-sd-platform.eliminate: For bridge or platform questions the distance is always train + platform, never one alone.
traps: Using only the platform length.
Forgetting the train's own length.
Not converting at the end.

q-sd-trains.cue: 'Two trains, 160 m and 140 m, run in opposite directions at 77 and 67 km/h. Time to cross?'
q-sd-trains.standard: Relative speed 77 + 67 = 144 km/h = 40 m/s; distance 160 + 140 = 300 m; time 7.5 s.
q-sd-trains.fast: Sum of lengths ÷ relative speed; with equal lengths and pole times t1, t2 the crossing time is 2 t1 t2 ÷ (t1 + t2).
q-sd-trains.eliminate: Opposite directions give a shorter time than either train passing a standing object of the other's length would.
traps: Subtracting the speeds when the trains run opposite ways.
Using one length only.

q-sd-average.cue: 'He goes at 12 km/h and returns at 4 km/h. Average speed?' or 'thirds of a journey at different speeds'.
q-sd-average.standard: Total distance ÷ total time; for equal distances 2 × 12 × 4 ÷ 16 = 6 km/h.
q-sd-average.fast: Equal distances: 2uv/(u + v). Equal times: simple average.
q-sd-average.eliminate: The average lies between the two speeds and is closer to the slower: strike the arithmetic mean (8).
traps: Taking the simple average of unequal-distance speeds.
Using the harmonic formula when the TIMES are equal.

q-sd-late.cue: 'At 5 km/h he is 6 minutes late, at 6 km/h 5 minutes early. Distance?'
q-sd-late.standard: Time gap = 6 + 5 = 11 minutes; D/5 − D/6 = 11/60, so D = 5.5 km.
q-sd-late.fast: D = (v1 × v2 ÷ speed gap) × time gap in hours; or test the options.
q-sd-late.eliminate: Late plus early minutes are ADDED: strike answers made with their difference.
traps: Subtracting the early minutes.
Mixing minutes with hours.

q-sd-race.cue: 'In a 1,000 m race A beats B by 100 m; in 400 m B beats C by 40 m. In 500 m A beats C by?'
q-sd-race.standard: A : B = 10 : 9 and B : C = 10 : 9 so A : C = 100 : 81. In 500 m C runs 405, so A wins by 95 m.
q-sd-race.fast: Chain the fractions 0.9 × 0.9 and apply to the distance.
q-sd-race.eliminate: A is faster than C by more than the A-B margin, so the answer exceeds 50 m: strike smaller options.
traps: Adding the margins (140 m) without scaling.
Using the wrong race length for the second ratio.
